answer: Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 118 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the copper seed, the signal timing is verifiable from the pigment record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 185 keys therefore forfeits 185 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
